I'd have to say it's a combination of a few factors.

Primarily it's the fact that every 4 years we have shady shit going on during caucuses (just look at Iowa this year on both sides) and there is outrage when it happens, but it's not sustained outrage because the next primary comes around and people have to focus on that or they'll get left behind.

Secondary, voter ID laws are passed in a public forum by legislatures in their official capacity as representatives of the people. Primaries and caucuses are run by the individual party committees and we've already seen the stranglehold the Democrats have on the process and how much the Republicans are trying to keep their stranglehold. Back in 2008 there were a few states (including Florida) that moved up their primaries to try and become more relevant and the DNC responded by invalidating all of the delegates from those states (later came back at half value for a compromise, iirc).

But to answer your question more succinctly, the Democratic establishment doesn't want Voter ID laws both because it disenfranchises voters, but ESPECIALLY Democratic voters. So it's in their best interest to fight against them. Likewise with the causus system, it favors the establishment candidates for both parties, so it's in their best interest to keep them in place.

And yes, I think caususes are bullshit and need to go. I also think voter ID laws are fine, as long as it's easy for voters to actually acquire that ID for free if they don't already have one. The problem with voter ID laws generally is they're accompanied by reduced hours at locations that issue the IDs or flat out closed locations. Similar to many of the abortion restriction laws which are getting passed now, they're crafted in such a way that aren't intended to make abortions safe, they're crafted in a way to make it virtually impossible to get an abortion.
